principles: Reviewer read claims must be machine-checkable and signed.
Mechanical evidence should be additive and should not make advisory memory/playbook output authoritative.
Missing required reviewer evidence must fail closed with actionable guidance.
The implementation must preserve scan escalation and role separation.
drivers: scope_check_save and review_pass_set are existing gate evidence writers and must stay deterministic.
The defined failure signal is an unrecorded full read of docs/requirements/decisions/*.md without scanEscalationReason.
The safest path is to reuse existing smoke and dispatch surfaces rather than introduce a broad new runtime subsystem.

options.name: shared-schema-plus-minimal-read-log
pros: One readManifest normalizer keeps scope and review evidence comparable.
Signed fields make missing or changed read claims detectable immediately.
A small mechanical read-log helper can be tested with fixtures before deeper dispatch retention work.
cons: Mechanical capture may start as fixture-backed evidence unless dispatch transcript retention is already available.
Some reviewer host implementations may need follow-up wiring for live transcript capture.

options.name: prompt-only-readManifest
pros: Fastest implementation and low risk to runtime dispatch.
cons: Still relies on self-report and does not solve the fa1777b proof gap.
Cannot flag self-report versus mechanical-log mismatch.

options.name: full-dispatch-rewrite
pros: Could capture every host read uniformly.
cons: Too broad for this story and high risk to active review gates.
Likely duplicates or destabilizes existing dispatch and host readiness work.

rationale: Use a shared signed schema for immediate gateable evidence, then add the smallest mechanical read-log/mismatch detector that can be validated independently. This solves the documented proof gap without expanding into a full dispatch rewrite.

preMortem.scenario: Existing reviewers can no longer submit evidence because templates are updated but commands reject old inputs abruptly.
preMortem.trigger: scope_check_save or review_pass_set requires readManifest without clear prompt guidance.
preMortem.consequence: Gate failures become confusing and slow reviewer workflows.
preMortem.mitigation: Update prompts/templates in the same story and add explicit rejection messages plus smoke coverage.

preMortem.scenario: readManifest is persisted but not signed, so it can be edited after the fact.
preMortem.trigger: The new field is saved outside the hash/signature domain.
preMortem.consequence: Read evidence appears first-class but is not integrity-bound.
preMortem.mitigation: Add signature/hash drift tests that change only readManifest and expect verification failure.

preMortem.scenario: Mechanical log blocks legitimate broad scans.
preMortem.trigger: Mismatch detector treats scanEscalationReason as invalid or blocks the escalation path.
preMortem.consequence: Reviewers avoid necessary reads or the gate becomes brittle.
preMortem.mitigation: Make mismatch/full-scan reporting a finding/surfacing path and preserve scan escalation semantics.

preMortem.scenario: JSON output becomes polluted with progress or diagnostics.
preMortem.trigger: New rejection or mismatch diagnostics write to stdout for --json commands.
preMortem.mitigation: Add JSON cleanliness assertions to the smoke.
